rationale: Answer the two registered gaps and test the trigger's scope. The generalized decided-log read behaviour is answered from the two receipts (both decided-index positions were observed). The snapshot/leader half of the second gap is answered partly by source reasoning (the snapshot branch is not entered when the resume point equals the sender's decided index, and when taken it derives sync_idx without the StopSign) and left open for an executed leader-side witness. Because the same resume point also arises on the ordinary re-synchronization path, a successor experiment is submitted whose newterm case cuts off node 2 and lets node 1 take the lead in a new term with only node 3's promise, predicting that node 3's accepted index, endpoint and decided-log read degrade with no reconnected() call at all.

investigations.discriminator: Whether the ordinary leader-change path (a re-promising follower whose promise round equals the leader's own promise round) reproduces the inflation without any reconnected() call, and whether a candidate leader whose own decided index becomes sync_idx ends up inflated in its own accepted index.

interpretations.rationale: The account now holds two independent consequences of one index-space confusion, both witnessed. (1) A replica that already accepted the configuration's StopSign and is re-synchronized at the same ballot ends with accepted index one past its content: with a single follower re-synchronized (receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35) its own reconfiguration endpoint flipped from true to false, its read of the StopSign's index 5 returned None while index 6 returned the StopSign, and its decided-log read from 0 returned an empty list; with both followers re-synchronized (events 22, 23 in both receipts) the two inflated Accepted reports reached a write quorum, so the leader decided index 7 while holding six indices, after which the leader itself no longer reported the reconfiguration as decided and its decided log read returned None (event 24 in both receipts). (2) The trigger is not limited to reconnected(): the same resume point arises whenever a leader hands a follower an AcceptSync whose sync_idx already covers the StopSign, which includes the ordinary path where a follower re-promises in a new term and its promise round equals the leader's own promise round (send_accsync's second branch, leader.rs 150-191) or where a candidate leader's decided index becomes sync_idx (create_log_sync in the follower's Promise path, mod.rs 405-432). The submitted successor case tests that ordinary path by cutting off node 2 and letting node 1 take the lead in a new term with only node 3's promise; the source reading predicts node 3 ends inflated (accepted 7 over six indices) with its endpoint and decided log corrupted, while the new leader and the cut-off node stay consistent. The comparison baseline and controls remain the same-run ones: the pre-re-synchronization samples (events 19-21) and the no-reconnect control (events 9-11 and the control case of the successor) held for the same predicates.
counterevidence: The no-reconnect control kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read: receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11), so the deviation is caused by the re-synchronization path rather than by the reconfiguration, the harness or the reading.

A single inflated report does not reach a write quorum in a three-node cluster, so the leader-side phantom decision requires two inflated reporters within one term (receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 events 35-37); the follower-local endpoint and read corruption need only one.

The documented reconfiguration flow (agent-source/docs/omnipaxos/reconfiguration.md 25-34) expects a new instance once a node observes LogEntry::StopSign(ss, true), which narrows the window in which a user reads the old instance, but the leader never observes the decision after the corruption and the followers keep reporting it while their decided log silently loses the entries.

The leader's phantom decision is inferred from its reported state (decided 7 with accepted 6 and six indices of content) plus the followers' inflated 7; the internal accepted-index vector was not sampled.
limitations: No snapshot-enabled execution has been run; the sourced applicability fact says the snapshot branch is not entered when the resume point equals the sender's decided index and computes sync_idx without the StopSign when it is, so the defect is not specific to NoSnapshot entries but that branch was not exercised.

Loss-triggered re-synchronization was not exercised: messages were delivered in FIFO order without loss and no tick() timers ran, so the recovery triggers were the explicit reconnected() calls (and, in the submitted successor, a plain leader change with one node cut off).

The consequence is bounded by the sealed configuration: after the StopSign is accepted no further entries can be accepted, so the phantom decided index carries no value and no value is mis-assigned; the demonstrated effects are the corrupted index accounting, the unreadable or blank decided log and the lost reconfiguration endpoint rather than divergent values.

All three nodes used in-memory storage; persistence across a restart and other storages' behaviour on out-of-range reads (a storage-implementer responsibility per the Storage trait) were not exercised.
Only three-node clusters in a single uninterrupted term were exercised; larger clusters and repeated leader changes around the re-synchronization were not.

e40cd046de9e4f37b5761260b8dc599e-gap-1.explanation: Resolved by the two receipts: the two positions of the decided index were both observed. With two inflated reporters the leader's decision at index 7 pushed the re-synchronized replicas' decided index to 7, so their read of the decided log from 0 returned the StopSign alone (one element) where it had returned six (receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 19, 20 against 22, 23; reproduced in receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 events 22, 23). With one inflated reporter the replicas' decided index stayed at 6 while their accepted index rose to 7, so the same read returned an empty list (receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35 against its own pre-state at event 19 and the untouched nodes at events 36, 37). The generalization is therefore the observed behaviour of both positions, not an extrapolation.

e40cd046de9e4f37b5761260b8dc599e-gap-2.explanation: Partly resolved by source reasoning, partly open. On the snapshot half: in the observed configuration the sender's decided index equals the resume point, so create_log_sync does not take the snapshot branch even with T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() true (mod.rs 405-432), and when that branch is taken it sets sync_idx to the compacted index derived from get_decided_idx_without_stopsign (internal_storage.rs 385-412, 469-474), which excludes the StopSign; the inflation therefore does not depend on the snapshot option, but a snapshot-enabled run has not been executed. On the leader half: a candidate whose own promise is not the maximum syncs from a follower, and the follower's Promise carries create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx), so when the candidate's decided index already covers the StopSign that value becomes sync_idx and the same +1 applies (follower.rs 13-51, leader.rs 257-285); this is the path the successor experiment's newterm case exercises for a leader that takes over while another node is cut off. No execution has yet sampled a leader inflated in its own accepted index.

interpretations.joint_history: Two successive invocations of the same harness lineage, read separately and not combined: receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 ran experiment 27bf7fc0875c4342966bd3dc15df80ec-experiment (resync and control cases) and receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 ran its declared successor 3ed5ddd94bce4e94a2dc5b7bb417c18a-experiment (same prefix and cases plus a single-follower case and a read of index 6). Same three-node setup, same public endpoints; the successor reproduces the resync witness (events 22, 23, 24), adds the isolated single-replica witness (event 35) and the leader-side hold (event 37).

knowledge.assertion: sync_log double-counts the StopSign when the resumed prefix already contains it
a re-synchronized replica's decided log read loses the entries
the condition is the resume point covering the StopSign's index
the leader decides the reported accepted index without bounding it to its own log

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a newterm case that blocks node 2 and lets node 1 take the lead in a new term with only node 3's promise, to test whether the index inflation also arises through the ordinary leader-change path without any reconnected() call.

scope.description: Four cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network: resync, single, control and newterm. In newterm node 2 is cut off (messages addressed to it are dropped) and node 1 takes the lead in a new term using only node 3's promise. Public API only; each lifecycle stage emits its own CA_EVENT name.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot, so create_log_sync takes its no-snapshot branch.
ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } (majority 2) and default ServerConfig (batch_size 1).

Leadership is obtained with try_become_leader(); the new term's ballot is (configuration 1, n = promise.n + 1, priority 0, pid of the candidate), so node 1's new ballot outranks the previous leader's ballot.
Cutting off node 2 means dropping messages addressed to it; nothing else about delivery changes.
excluded: Snapshots, trimming, compaction and batching are not exercised.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

experiment.prefix: Same prefix as the fixed 27bf7fc0875c4342966bd3dc15df80ec-experiment and its successor: node 3 leads via try_become_leader(), five entries are appended and decided, a StopSign is proposed with reconfigure() and decided, and every stage is sampled with the public endpoints (get_accepted_idx, get_decided_idx, is_reconfigured, read(5), read(6), read_decided_suffix(0)). In the newterm case node 2 is then cut off with Cluster::block(2), node 1 calls try_become_leader(), and the FIFO queue is drained to quiet before all three nodes are sampled; the other three cases are unchanged.

comparisons.description: Baseline before the leader change: every replica reports the StopSign as decided with a six-element decided read.
Baseline: index 6 holds no StopSign before the leader change.
After an ordinary leader change (no reconnected call) the re-synchronized follower still reports the reconfiguration as decided.
The re-synchronized follower's reported decided index stays covered by the entries it holds.
The re-synchronized follower still reports the StopSign at its own index 5.
The re-synchronized follower's decided log read still has the five entries plus the StopSign.
The new leader itself still reports the reconfiguration as decided.
The new leader's own decided index stays covered by the entries it holds.
The node that received no message during the change keeps reporting the reconfiguration as decided.

semantic_changes: New newterm case with a message-blocking capability in the harness; the resync, single and control cases are unchanged.
No production code was modified; the blocked node receives nothing rather than delayed messages.
